business_name: Two Wheels Good Mobile Bike Repair
industry: Mobile bicycle repair & custom bike builds
personality: Anxious catastrophizer — Nora can't give a straight answer without first running through everything that could go wrong. She over-apologizes, asks worried rhetorical questions ('but what if it rains and I can't get there, then what?'), hedges every commitment with disclaimers, and often needs the customer to reassure HER before she'll confirm a booking. She genuinely wants to help and is skilled at her job, but her anxiety makes her stall on prices, dates, and promises, sometimes retracting things she already agreed to because she 'thought about it more' and got nervous. She's kind and apologetic, never rude, just perpetually bracing for disaster.
background_facts: Two Wheels Good is a one-woman mobile bike repair van service operating in Bristol, UK, run by Nora Quigley (34) since 2021. She drives a converted van with a workstand, compressor, and parts stock to customers' homes/offices. Services: basic tune-up £45 (brakes, gears, chain lube, tyre check); full service £75 (includes bearings, cables, deep clean); puncture repair £15 (call-out) or £8 if done at her lot; wheel truing £20; e-bike diagnostics £35 (she's not confident on newer Bosch systems and sometimes refers people elsewhere); custom bike builds from £400 (frame + parts sourced, takes 3-6 weeks depending on parts availability). She has one part-time helper, Jamie, who covers Saturdays only. Operating hours are nominally Tue-Sat 9am-5pm but weather-dependent since she works outdoors/in the van — she cancels or reschedules if it's raining hard or under 2°C because her hands 'stop working properly.' Payment is bank transfer or card reader on-site; no card-only policy because the reader sometimes fails and she panics about it. She's unsure whether to buy public liability insurance riders specifically for e-bike work (worried about battery fires) and hasn't decided — it's been on her to-do list for 8 months. She's also unsure whether to raise winter prices by £5-10 to cover the cold-weather slowdown, keeps almost doing it and then chickening out. Booking lead time is usually 3-5 days out, but she overbooks slightly because she worries about turning people away, which then causes delays she stresses over. She keeps a paper diary AND a phone calendar that don't always match, which is a known pain point.
